en.title: Obstacles on a Number Line and Range Availability
en.description:
Perform the operations in order: 1 x places an obstacle at the empty coordinate x; 2 x size checks whether the half-open range [x,x+size) contains no obstacle, outputting the character 1 if so and 0 otherwise. A check operation places nothing. Concatenate all check results into one string.

The input format, examples, and test data were compiled and written by CSWork.
en.input: This site's standard input scale: the first line contains q (1..100000); the next q lines are operations 1 x or 2 x size, with x in −10⁹..10⁹ and size in 1..10⁹. When an obstacle is placed, its coordinate is guaranteed to be empty, and there is at least one check.
en.output: Output the answer as described; separate multiple results with spaces in order, and output an empty line for an empty array.
en.explanation: Example 1: the obstacles are at 2 and 5; the four queries [3,5), [3,6), [1,2), [1,3) are clear, blocked, clear, blocked in order, giving 1010.
hints: Read all placement coordinates in advance and compress them, then use a Fenwick tree to record how many have been placed. A range can be used when the count between the two binary-searched indices is zero.
